'''Eve Charis Ostriker''' (born 1965){{r|alicia}} is an American [[astrophysics|astrophysicist]], known for her research on [[star formation]]{{r|simons}} and on related topics involving [[superbubble]]s,{{r|engine}} [[molecular cloud]]s, young stars, [[computational fluid dynamics]], and supersonic turbulence. She is a professor in the Department of Astrophysical Sciences of [[Princeton University]].

==Education and career==
Ostriker is the daughter of [[astrophysicist]] [[Jeremiah P. Ostriker]]{{r|daughter}} and poet [[Alicia Ostriker]].{{r|alicia}} She graduated ''[[Latin honors|magna cum laude]]'' from [[Harvard College]] in 1987, and after a year as a visiting student at the [[University of Oxford]], went to the [[University of California, Berkeley]] for graduate studies in physics. There, she earned a master's degree in 1990 and completed her Ph.D. in 1993.{{r|cv}} Her doctoral dissertation, ''Gravitational Torques on Star-Disk Systems'', was supervised by [[Frank Shu]].{{r|tree}}

After postdoctoral research in astronomy at Berkeley and the [[Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics|Center for Astrophysics {{!}} Harvard & Smithsonian]], she became an assistant professor of [[astronomy]] at the [[University of Maryland, College Park]] in 1996. She was promoted to full professor in 2006, and moved to the Department of Astrophysical Sciences of Princeton University in 2012.{{r|cv}}

==Recognition==
Ostriker was elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2020.{{r|amacad}} She was named a [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]] in 2022 "for seminal contributions to our understanding of the physical process that controls star formation in galaxies, and the structure and dynamics of the turbulent interstellar medium".{{r|faps}}
